edges.description: Truncated HOXA2 protein cannot activate the distant HMX1 enhancer it normally binds.
edges.target: Impaired Transactivation of the Long-Range HMX1 Enhancer

edges.description: HOXA2 is the selector gene that assigns second-arch identity to the cranial neural crest cells populating that arch; without it they adopt first-arch identity.
edges.target: Loss of Second Pharyngeal Arch Neural Crest Identity

edges.description: A route that does not run through the pharyngeal arches at all. Hoxa2 is expressed in the palate itself, and knocking it down there reduces the rate at which the shelves fuse. The intermediates the authors name - increased cell proliferation, and de-repression of the Hoxa2 targets Msx1, Bmp4, Barx1 and Ptx1 - are candidates they identify but do not trace to the fusion failure.
Reduced HMX1 activation is the candidate route from the HOXA2 alleles to the external ear defect; the link to the human auricle phenotype is inferred, not measured in patient tissue.
edges.source: Impaired Transactivation of the Long-Range HMX1 Enhancer

edges.description: Mis-specified second-arch crest builds first-arch structures instead of second-arch ones.
edges.source: Loss of Second Pharyngeal Arch Neural Crest Identity
edges.target: Homeotic Transformation of Second-Arch Skeletal Derivatives

edges.description: The pinna is built by the HOXA2-expressing second-arch neural crest mesenchyme, so loss of that identity removes the auricular program.
edges.source: Loss of Second Pharyngeal Arch Neural Crest Identity

edges.description: The same rhombencephalic neural crest that builds the craniofacial skeleton also patterns the craniofacial muscles, and Hoxa2 mutants have abnormal attachments and trajectories of the extrinsic tongue and hyoid muscles. How the arch-identity lesion produces that particular mis-routing was not worked out, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown.
edges.source: Loss of Second Pharyngeal Arch Neural Crest Identity
edges.target: Mis-Attachment of the Extrinsic Tongue and Hyoid Muscles

edges.description: Malformation of the middle-ear ossicular chain, a second- and first-arch derivative, is the developmental basis of the conductive component of the hearing loss.
edges.source: Homeotic Transformation of Second-Arch Skeletal Derivatives

edges.description: In the recessive subtype the hearing loss is characterised as mixed, and the same ossicular malformation accounts for its conductive half. Only that half follows from this node. The sensorineural half has no published mechanistic account in either the human family or the mouse models, which is the subject of the hoxa2_sensorineural_component_unexplained discussion; the edge is drawn to the mixed phenotype because that is how the recessive family's audiology is reported, not because this node explains both components.
edges.source: Homeotic Transformation of Second-Arch Skeletal Derivatives

edges.description: Failure of pinna morphogenesis presents clinically as bilateral microtia.

Barrow and Capecchi's interpretation of the correlation: the hyoglossus, unable to reach the greater horn, cannot depress the lateral edges of the tongue. Support for the link is the rescue arm - restoring the attachment in Hoxa1/Hoxa2 double mutants restores palatal closure over a flattened tongue - rather than direct observation of tongue posture in the single mutants.
edges.source: Mis-Attachment of the Extrinsic Tongue and Hyoid Muscles
edges.target: Abnormal Tongue Posture Obstructing Palatal Shelf Closure

edges.description: Shelves that do not close leave a cleft. In Hoxa1/Hoxa2 double mutants, where the hyoglossus attachment is restored, the penetrance of cleft palate falls sharply - the experimental result that ties the obstruction to the cleft.

edges.description: Shelves that fuse at a reduced rate leave a cleft. The measurement behind this edge is an explant fusion rate rather than a cleft count in vivo, and the authors' own claim is the weaker one - that the null cleft is not solely attributable to the tongue.
The model defines the identity-assignment lesion this node represents.

edges.description: Reproduces the skeletal consequence of the arch-identity lesion, including the middle-ear element that underlies the conductive hearing loss.

edges.description: Cleft palate is constant in the mouse null and matches the recessive human subtype.
edges.limitations: The mouse cleft is complete and lethal, whereas the human recessive subtype has a partial cleft and normal survival; and the dominant human subtype has no cleft at all.

edges.description: Loss of Hoxa1 on the Hoxa2-mutant background restores normal attachment of the hyoglossus to the greater horn of the hyoid.
edges.limitations: The rescue is by a second mutation rather than by restoring Hoxa2 or by any treatment, so it establishes that the palate depends on the attachment without showing how the attachment is normally specified. It is also a mouse result with no human counterpart.

edges.description: Restoring the hyoglossus attachment sharply reduces the penetrance of cleft palate, which is the experimental support for treating the muscle defect as causal rather than coincidental.
edges.limitations: Penetrance falls but the abstract does not report how far, and the rescue is genetic. It also does not exclude the palate-intrinsic route reported by Smith and colleagues, which was measured in explant culture rather than in this model.

edges.description: The late-inactivation arm is the closest available model of the human auricular phenotype, and the fate-mapping arm establishes the second-arch origin of the pinna that the mechanism depends on.
edges.limitations: Mouse and human pinna morphology differ substantially, and the model's resemblance to the human condition is the authors' assessment rather than a quantified comparison.

nodes.description: The proposed mechanical consequence, stated by its authors as a suggestion rather than an observation: with the hyoglossus unable to depress the lateral edges of the tongue, the tongue adopts an abnormal posture that blocks closure of the palatal shelves. It is not the only published account of the Hoxa2 cleft - see the hoxa2_cleft_palate_tongue_versus_intrinsic_palate discussion and the Intrinsic Palatal Shelf Fusion Defect node - and neither account has been tested in a human patient.

evidence.reference_title: Compensatory defects associated with mutations in Hoxa1 restore normal palatogenesis to Hoxa2 mutants.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that the hyoglossus, whose function is to depress the lateral edges of the tongue, when unable to make its proper attachment to the greater horn of the hyoid, forces the tongue to adopt an abnormal posture which blocks closure of the palatal shelves.

nodes.description: Staged surgical reconstruction of the external ear, using autologous costal cartilage or an alloplastic framework, is the standard management of bilateral microtia. No HOXA2-specific surgical series exists; management follows general microtia practice.

The defining feature and the only one present in every reported family: bilateral malformation or reduction of the external ear. It is bilateral in all reported pedigrees, recessive and dominant alike.

nodes.description: Surgical closure of the palatal cleft (palatoplasty), relevant only to the biallelic recessive subtype, in which partial cleft palate is reported. It is undertaken in infancy to protect feeding, middle-ear ventilation and speech development, and is the standard of care for cleft palate of any cause. No HOXA2-specific surgical series exists; management follows general cleft-palate practice.

Stage-specific conditional inactivation separates the auricular phenotype from the lethal null. Early inactivation abolishes the auricle and duplicates the external auditory canal; late inactivation yields a hypomorphic auricle that the authors take to mimic the human HOXA2 mutant condition. The reciprocal gain-of-function experiment - ectopic Hoxa2 in first-arch crest - duplicates the pinna and eliminates the canal.

The auricle fails to form normally. Timing determines severity in the mouse: early Hoxa2 inactivation abolishes the auricle and duplicates the external auditory canal, while late inactivation leaves a hypomorphic auricle resembling the human phenotype. Hoxa2 acts on pinna morphogenesis partly through BMP signalling and Eya1 expression.

animal_models.description: The late-inactivation arm is the closest available model of the human auricular phenotype, and the fate-mapping arm establishes the second-arch origin of the pinna that the mechanism depends on.
animal_models.genotype: Conditional Hoxa2 inactivation at early versus late gestational stages, plus conditional ectopic Hoxa2 in first-arch neural crest

evidence.reference_title: Mouse Hoxa2 mutations provide a model for microtia and auricle duplication.
evidence.snippet: In mice, Hoxa2 inactivation at early gestational stages results in external auditory canal (EAC) duplication and absence of the auricle, whereas its late inactivation results in a hypomorphic auricle, mimicking the human HOXA2 mutant condition.

evidence.reference_title: Mouse Hoxa2 mutations provide a model for microtia and auricle duplication.
evidence.snippet: Hoxa2 partly controls the morphogenesis of the pinna through the BMP signalling pathway and expression of Eya1, which in humans is involved in branchio-oto-renal syndrome.

nodes.description: Two allele classes have been reported. Heterozygous nonsense alleles (p.Lys213*, p.Glu224*, p.Gln235*) truncate the protein and act by haploinsufficiency. The recessive allele is instead a homeodomain missense, p.Q186K, at a highly conserved residue; homology modelling predicts the mutant lysine side chain sits further from a nearby phosphate group, losing a hydrogen bond and impairing DNA binding.

evidence.reference_title: HOXA2 haploinsufficiency in dominant bilateral microtia and hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing of affected family members detected only seven shared, rare, heterozygous, nonsynonymous variants, including one protein truncating variant, a HOXA2 nonsense change (c.703C>T, p.Q235*).

evidence.snippet: Subsequent DNA sequence analysis of the HOXA1 and HOXA2 homeobox genes from the candidate region identified an interesting HOXA2 homeodomain variant: a change in a highly conserved amino acid (p.Q186K).

evidence.snippet: In the model of the mutant homeodomain, the position of the mutant lysine side chain is consistently farther away from a nearby phosphate group; this altered position results in the loss of a hydrogen bond and affects the DNA-binding activity.

evidence.snippet: Next generation sequencing identified two heterozygous nonsense HOXA2 mutations, one in each family.

Hearing impairment is present in the recessive family and in some but not all dominant families; where characterised it is mixed, symmetrical and severe to profound. The published series describe the dominant phenotype as microtia "with or without hearing impairment", so it is a variable feature of that subtype.

evidence.snippet: To date, only four HOXA2 mutations were reported in families with autosomal-recessive or dominant microtia, with or without hearing impairment.

nodes.description: In the mouse null, second-arch skeletal elements are absent and are replaced by duplicated first-arch structures, including duplicated ossification centres of the middle-ear bones and a second Meckel's cartilage beside the otic capsule. Because the middle-ear ossicles are second- and first-arch derivatives, this is the developmental origin of the conductive component of the hearing impairment.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of stained skeletons revealed that homozygous mutant animals contained multiple cranial skeletal defects, including a duplication of the ossification centers of the bones of the middle ear.

nodes.description: An independent null allele reported simultaneously. Homozygotes are born with cleft palate and die within 24 hours, with duplicated middle-ear ossification centres and a second Meckel's cartilage beside the otic capsule.

A single allele disrupting both linked genes, analysed against the single mutants. Some double-mutant craniofacial defects are additive combinations of the single-mutant ones and others appear only in the double mutant. The result that matters here is a rescue: compensatory defects associated with loss of Hoxa1 restore the hyoglossus attachment that is blocked in Hoxa2 mutants, and the penetrance of cleft palate falls sharply.

The original targeted disruption. Homozygotes die at birth. Rhombomeric segmentation and neural crest migration are normal, but second-arch mesenchymal crest derivatives are missing and the surviving second-arch crest is transformed to first-arch identity, establishing Hoxa2 as the second-arch selector gene.

Hoxa2 binds a long-range enhancer of Hmx1 in the mouse - Hmx1 is itself a transcription factor required for eye and ear development - and both reported Chinese nonsense alleles fail to activate that enhancer in reporter assays. This is the one HOXA2 target so far tied experimentally to the human microtia alleles.

evidence.snippet: In mouse, Hoxa2 can bind to a long-range enhancer and regulate expression of the Hmx1 gene, which is a crucial transcription factor in eye and ear development.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of loss-of-function HOXA2 mutations in Chinese families with dominant bilateral microtia.
evidence.snippet: Our results also provide molecular insights about how these nonsense HOXA2 mutations could affect the activation of its downstream target HMX1 by interacting with the long-range enhancer.

nodes.description: A second, independent route to the same cleft. Hoxa2 is expressed in the developing palate itself between E12.5 and E15.5, and Hoxa2-null palatal shelves cultured in the absence of the tongue fuse at lower rates than heterozygous or wild-type shelves, as do shelves in which Hoxa2 is knocked down with antisense constructs. Null palates show an overall increase in cell proliferation, and Hoxa2 represses Msx1, Bmp4, Barx1 and Ptx1 within the palate. On the authors' reading the mouse cleft is therefore not solely secondary to the tongue. Whether either route operates in HOXA2-mutant humans is unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Hoxa2 plays a direct role in murine palate development.
evidence.snippet: we detected Hoxa2 expression in the developing palate at both the mRNA and protein levels between embryonic day (E) 12.5 and E15.5

evidence.reference_title: Hoxa2 plays a direct role in murine palate development.
evidence.snippet: Organ cultures of Hoxa2(-/-) palates maintained in the absence of the tongue showed decreased fusion rates than either Hoxa2(+/-) or Hoxa2(+/+) palate cultures.

evidence.reference_title: Hoxa2 plays a direct role in murine palate development.
evidence.snippet: These results demonstrate the cleft palate phenotype of Hoxa2 null embryos is not solely due to abnormal tongue musculature, and indicate a direct role of Hoxa2 in regulating murine palatogenesis.

nodes.description: In Hoxa2-null mice, rhombomeric segmentation and neural crest migration are intact, but the mesenchymal neural crest derivatives of the second arch are missing and the surviving second-arch mesenchymal crest adopts first-arch identity. The lesion is one of identity assignment rather than of crest generation or survival - which distinguishes it from the ribosome-biogenesis neurocristopathies that conform to the same module node.

evidence.reference_title: A homeotic transformation is generated in the rostral branchial region of the head by disruption of Hoxa-2, which acts as a selector gene.
evidence.snippet: While rhombomeric and neural crest cell (NCC) segmentation was not affected, mesenchymal NCC derivatives of the second arch were lacking, and second arch mesenchymal NCC identity was changed to first arch identity, resulting in homeotic transformation of second to first arch skeletal elements.

nodes.description: In Hoxa2 mutant mice the attachments and trajectories of the extrinsic tongue and hyoid muscles are abnormal. The abnormal trajectory of two of them, the styloglossus and the stylohyoideus, blocks the attachment of the hyoglossus to the greater horn of the hyoid, and that blocked attachment correlated exactly with the presence of cleft palate in those animals. The node is mouse-derived; no comparable observation has been reported in HOXA2-mutant patients, in whom tongue and hyoid muscle anatomy has not been described.

The conductive component is attributable to the ossicular malformation; the sensorineural component is not mechanistically accounted for by any published human or mouse observation.
